original_question: Let X be a non-hyperelliptic curve, and let θ: SU_X(2) \dashrightarrow |2Θ| be the theta map sending a rank-2 semistable bundle E with trivial determinant to the divisor { L in J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X, E ⊗ L) ≥ 1 }. Is this map always an embedding?
target_in_paper: Section 4 (Rank 2), Q4, immediately after Theorem 4(c): “Is θ always an embedding for C non hyperelliptic?” This is the exact open problem your draft is trying to capture. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the rank-2 theta map on SU_X(2), the non-hyperelliptic case, the divisor-valued definition E ↦ {L ∈ J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X,E⊗L) ≥ 1}, and the precise issue Beauville leaves open—whether the map is an embedding. This matches the paper’s definition of θ in §2 and the open question Q4 in §4. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works with X a compact Riemann surface of genus g, not an unspecified curve over an arbitrary field. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

The genus restriction should be made explicit: Q4 concerns the non-hyperelliptic case of Theorem 4(c), so effectively g ≥ 3, since the genus-2 case is treated separately in Theorem 4(a). ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

SU_X(2) should be described as the moduli space of S-equivalence classes of semistable rank-2 vector bundles with trivial determinant. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

J^{g-1}(X)=Pic^{g-1}(X) and the canonical theta divisor Θ ⊂ J^{g-1}(X), given by Θ={M ∈ J^{g-1}(X) | H^0(X,M) ≠ 0}, should be defined explicitly. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

In rank 2 the map is actually an everywhere-defined morphism, because Theorem 3(a) says |𝓛| has no base points; the paper’s open problem is therefore not about whether a rational map extends. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
The quantifier in “always” should be stated explicitly: for every non-hyperelliptic X. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

To align exactly with the paper, one should note that θ is identified with the morphism φ_𝓛 defined by the determinant bundle 𝓛 via Theorem 2. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 3 that is not hyperelliptic. Let SU_X(2) be the moduli space of S-equivalence classes of semistable rank-2 vector bundles with trivial determinant, let J^{g-1}(X)=Pic^{g-1}(X), and let Θ ⊂ J^{g-1}(X) be the canonical theta divisor. For a moduli point [E] ∈ SU_X(2), define Θ_E := { M ∈ J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X,E⊗M) ≥ 1 }. In rank 2 this gives an everywhere-defined theta morphism θ: SU_X(2) → |2Θ|. Is θ an embedding for every non-hyperelliptic X? ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, via the canonical isomorphism H^0(SU_X(2),𝓛) ≅ H^0(J^{g-1}(X),O(2Θ))^* of Theorem 2, is the morphism φ_𝓛: SU_X(2) → |𝓛|^* defined by the determinant bundle 𝓛 an embedding for every non-hyperelliptic X? Beauville explicitly says that, in rank 2, studying φ_𝓛 amounts to studying θ. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Q4 in §4, posed immediately after Theorem 4(c). The surrounding context needed to make it stand-alone is spread across §1–§4: §1 defines X, J^{g-1}(X), Θ, and SU_X(r); §2 defines the theta map θ and identifies it with the determinant-linear-system map φ_𝓛; §3 proves that for r=2 there are no base points, so θ is a morphism; and §4 states the known cases and then asks exactly whether θ is always an embedding in the non-hyperelliptic rank-2 case. Your draft is close, but it should replace the dashed arrow by a morphism, quantify “always,” and make the ambient complex-curve and moduli-space notation explicit. ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))
